selected.rationale: 100% packet loss on webapp->ordering-api breaks the synchronous checkout call; no bounded timeout/retry leaves order placement hanging or failing with availability loss.
Injecting delay on webapp->ordering-api tests unbounded latency propagation on the critical order path; without a per-request timeout the user request is held until the client deadline.
Loss on webapp->basket-api makes the cart unavailable during checkout; no fallback or retry turns a cart read/update into a user-visible failure.
Delayed order-db access propagates latency into every Ordering.API call and can exhaust the connection pool; missing DB timeout/retry is a likely confirmed weakness.
Loss on the mobile order-submission edge causes the mobile checkout to fail or hang; the BFF lacks a retry/degradation path for the ordering dependency.
Redis is the basket state store; losing this edge breaks cart persistence, and the absence of a fallback makes checkout unable to proceed.
A delayed RabbitMQ publish from webapp couples a non-critical event bus to the primary user flow; without async decoupling or timeout, requests hang (dependency isolation defect).
Losing the order-started event on ordering-api->rabbitmq means OrderProcessor never starts fulfillment; without outbox/retry, orders stay stuck.
Dropping payment-result events leaves order/payment state inconsistent; the system has no reliable delivery/retry for a critical payment message.
Identity is a shared authentication dependency; loss on webapp->identity-api breaks login/session checks with no degradation, exposing missing retry/circuit breaking.
